title: A held-out file of real questions answers at a recorded rate, and never feeds the eval set
goal: kb/public/_retrieval/lookup_heldout.csv holds 20 questions worded as real sessions asked them (taken from the query log store's lookup records, placeholders for private names), none of which is a lookup_eval.csv row or a doc2query expansion; rag.py eval --min N exits 0 when at least N rows pass and 1 otherwise, so python3 _tools/rag.py eval --file kb/public/_retrieval/lookup_heldout.csv --root public --min N is the kb's answer-rate fitness test; a failing held-out row stays in the file and is never moved into lookup_eval.csv or expanded on, so the file stays held out (kb/_self/maintaining.md states the exception to Real misses feed the eval set); and the rate N and the date it was last measured are stated in kb/_self/tools.md

gates.question: What answer rate on the 20 held-out questions calls the kb ready?
options: 14 of 20 (70%, the rate the earlier held-out run reached)

notes: Premise (quality of answers, held-out): before a sprint commits this story, draft the 20 rows from the query log store's lookup records and run python3 _tools/rag.py eval --file <draft> --root public once; record passed= here. Earlier held-out run (SP-njilrify, ST-dvf3xf52): 14 of 20 answered with verdict good on all 20. The tuned set passes 273 of 273 on 2026-10-07 (python3 _tools/rag.py eval --root public), so only a held-out set measures anything. Threshold N: see the gate. Premise run 2026-10-08 (plan step 6): a 20-row draft from the committed store's lookup records (87 candidates after dropping eval-set duplicates and kb/_self rule questions), expected path = the record's best article: python3 _tools/rag.py eval --file <scratch>/lookup_heldout_draft.csv --root public gave questions=20 passed=19 verdict_ok=20 found_ok=19 (HO-msbuild-getproperty: verdict good, no article found for agents/codebase-mapping.csv). Caveat the goal must state: these questions were asked before and researched since (46 of 87 were judged missed at the time), so the file is held out from lookup_eval.csv and doc2query, not from research; the worker words the rows as asked, verifies each expected path by reading the article, and prefers questions whose research closed after 2026-10-01 or whose verdict was good when asked. Checks (precheck 2026-10-08): the --min 16 held-out check fails before the work (no --min flag, no file) and is the proof; rag.py eval --root public and tests.py -k eval pin that the tuned set and the eval tests keep passing after the flag lands.
